applicable_conditions: When testing sensitivity of J-15 launch timing in a defended environment.
When the enemy point-defense system has consistent effectiveness against small salvos.
When the J-15 missile type is the same and range/altitude unchanged.
counter_conditions: If the timing difference is large (minutes) such that surface strikes have depleted defenses.
If the J-15s are launched from different directions or altitudes.
If the missile type is changed to one with better penetration.
hypothesis: Shifting J-15 launch delay by 5 seconds does not improve weapon effectiveness; earlier J-15 release (at 00:35:29 vs 00:36:39) produced identical misses, indicating that J-15 missile hits are not sensitive to small timing changes.

details: Minimum viable timing adjustments should be at least 60 seconds.
Coordinate J-15 release to coincide with the second wave of surface missiles after defensive expenditure.
Test timing changes only when other variables (fire quantity, target) are held constant.
recommended_pattern.summary: Do not expect 5-10 second changes in J-15 launch delay to affect hit probability; instead focus on salvo size or coordination with surface attacks.
